key_insight: LLM-generated SQL enabled rapid, explicit screening for potential cancer trial eligibility, with 95.8% agreement against physician consensus.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help identify trials for clinician review, but it does not establish full eligibility or guide treatment selection.
method: Converted unstructured trial criteria into reusable SQL eligibility rules.
Structured 24 synthetic patient vignettes for rule-based matching without further LLM inference.
Screened 746 recruiting US trials for advanced breast, colon, and non-small cell lung cancers.
evidence_signal: Across 240 patient–trial pairs from 10 trials, agreement was 230/240, sensitivity 83.3%, and specificity 100%; screening all 746 trials took a median 0.459 seconds per patient, excluding data preparation.
watch_item: Validation used synthetic patients and omitted laboratory results and comorbidities; missed matches highlight the need for further validation.
paper_title: Quantifying Cancer Clinical Trial Eligibility Using Artificial Intelligence-Based Matching
